content.title: FOOD FACTS THAT SOUND MADE UP BUT AREN'T
facts: **Cashews** never grow inside a shell like most nuts — each one dangles at the bottom of a cashew apple, fully exposed to the air.
**Nutmeg** contains a compound similar to a mild hallucinogen — eating just 2 whole nutmegs can cause hours of disorientation, which is why it's never sold ground in bulk.
**Bananas** are naturally slightly radioactive because of their potassium content — you'd need to eat around 10 million at once for it to matter.
**Strawberries** aren't technically berries, but bananas and avocados are — botanically, a true berry just needs seeds embedded in the flesh.
**Almonds** are actually seeds from a fruit related to peaches, not true nuts — the fuzzy green outer flesh is simply tossed aside during harvest.
**Carrots** were originally purple or white — the familiar orange color only became common a few centuries ago after selective breeding in the Netherlands.
**Peanuts** grow underground even though they hang on stems above soil while flowering — after pollination, the stem bends down and buries the pod itself.
**Pineapples** contain an enzyme called bromelain that actively digests proteins — it's technically breaking down your tongue a little every time you eat one.

content.caption:
A few of these deserve extra explaining. Nutmeg's disorienting effect comes from a compound called myristicin, which your liver converts into something structurally close to amphetamine — your body basically can't process large amounts safely, which is exactly why it's always sold pre-ground in tiny amounts. Pineapples stay soft-fleshed and never fully "set" in gelatin because that same bromelain enzyme keeps breaking down proteins even after you swallow it, which is also why your mouth can feel slightly raw after eating a lot at once. And almonds sit in the same botanical family as peaches and cherries because they all develop from a fleshy fruit around a hard pit — we just crack open the pit and eat the seed inside instead of the flesh. Nutrition is full of these strange, verifiable details.
